# Philadelphia Mint

The Philadelphia Mint, the nation's first, was established in 1794 and
struck the earliest federal coinage in a converted whiskey distillery
on Seventh Street.

Philadelphia coins traditionally carry no mintmark, a convention that
held until the wartime nickels of 1942 and was only fully abandoned in
1979 when the P mintmark spread to circulating denominations.

The facility has moved four times; the current building on Independence
Mall opened in 1969 and remains the largest mint in the world by
production capacity.
